name: Run an administrative operation
description: Executes one administrative operation with the venue's authority. Odin only. Without `user`, only what your own caps cannot do: v/ops/user/delete (never the owner's own account or a user another god keeps), v/ops/user/authentication-revoke (a user's sign-in key), v/ops/mcp/add-server|remove-server|refresh|tools-list (the venue's MCP servers, which reach local hosts and use the venue's secrets), and v/ops/ucan/issue (grants over venue-controlled resources, signed as the venue). The rest of the venue's administration — users, adapters and modules, peers, its secrets, storage, restart, relaunch, shutdown — you call directly, under your own caps. With `user`: runs the operation inside that user's namespace on their behalf (user:sudo, this venue's own users only) — one of v/ops/covia/read|list|inspect|slice|aggregate|write|copy|delete, v/ops/agent/create|list|info|update|suspend|resume|reload-context|sessions|compact-session|rename-session|delete-session|delete, v/ops/skills/list|read|import, v/ops/brightside/delete-skill, v/ops/secret/list|set|delete. Without `user`, v/ops/job/cancel with the `id` of an Inbox request Odin made itself withdraws it, once it no longer needs an answer; no other job. Anything else is refused: answering an Inbox, talking to an agent as its owner, scheduling or running other operations, money, and the venue's own agents. Every run is a recorded job.

operation.description: The full operation path, e.g. v/ops/venue/adapter/enable.

input.description: The operation's own input, exactly as its schema describes.

user.description: Optional: a user DID of this venue. When present the operation runs inside that user's namespace on their behalf, and must be one of the namespace operations.
